title: Presheaf stalk of sectionwise extension of scalars
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $R_1,R_2$ sheaves of commutative rings, $\alpha:R_1\to R_2$ a morphism and $x\in X$. For each sheaf $F$ of $R_1$-modules, let $P_F$ be the presheaf of $R_2$-modules $U\mapsto R_2(U)\otimes_{R_1(U)}F(U)$ with tensor restrictions [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. There exists a family of $R_{2,x}$-linear isomorphisms $\Psi_F:R_{2,x}\otimes_{R_{1,x}}F_x\longrightarrow (P_F)_x$, where the scalar action is induced by $\alpha_x$ and stalks use [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], such that $\Psi_F(a_x\otimes s_x)=(a\otimes s)_x$ for every neighborhood $U$ of $x$, $a\in R_2(U)$ and $s\in F(U)$.

source.place: Tag 007K, label lemma-stalk-tensor-presheaf-modules; the source omits the proof, supplied here from varying-ring tensor colimits.

proof.text: Construct the additive natural transformation F(U) → R₂(U) tensor over R₁(U) F(U), s ↦ 1 tensor s. Naturality follows from the characterized tensor restrictions in changeOfRingsMap. Take its additive stalk map h. For scalar and vector germs restrict to a common neighborhood; germ_smul and the stalk map formula for α show h is linear from F_x to the restriction of (P_F)_x along α_x. The extend/restrict scalars adjunction gives an R₂,x-linear map ψ_F. On a tensor of germs on U its value is germ(a) times germ(1 tensor s), hence germ(a tensor s).

Construct an additive left inverse Q of ψ_F by the stalk colimit universal property. On a neighborhood U the two germ maps are semilinear over the ring germ R₁(U) → R₁,x; semilinearity of the coefficient germ follows from α_x(germ(r)) = germ(α_U(r)). TensorProduct.map therefore gives an additive map from P_F(U) to R₂,x tensor over R₁,x F_x. These maps commute with restrictions: check on pure tensors using the restriction formula and germ_res_apply, then use tensor induction. They give a cocone on the neighborhood diagram and hence colimit.desc gives Q. On a pure tensor of arbitrary stalk elements, choose section representatives and restrict both to a common neighborhood. The germ formula for ψ_F and the defining equation for colimit.desc give Q(ψ_F(a tensor s)) = a tensor s. Tensor induction gives the left inverse identity on all tensors, proving injectivity.

Every element of (P_F)_x has a section representative t in P_F(U). Induct on the section tensor t. Zero lifts to zero, a pure tensor a tensor s lifts to the tensor of its germs by the formula for ψ_F, and a sum lifts to the sum of the lifts. Thus ψ_F is surjective. Use LinearEquiv.ofBijective and toModuleIso for each F. Its forward map is ψ_F, so its germ formula is exactly the one already proved.

theorem stalkChangeOfRingsPresheafIso (X : TopCat.{u})
    (R₁ R₂ : Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) CommRingCat.{u})
    (α : R₁ ⟶ R₂) (x : X) :
    ∃ Φ : ∀ F : SheafOfModules.{u}
        ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
          (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R₁),
      (ModuleCat.extendScalars ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map α.hom).hom).obj
        (ModuleCat.of (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₁.obj x)
          (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) F.val.presheaf x)) ≅
      ModuleCat.of (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₂.obj x)
        (TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) (changeOfRingsPresheaf α F).presheaf x),
      (∀ (F : SheafOfModules.{u}
          ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
            (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R₁))
        (U : Opens X) (hx : x ∈ U) (s : F.val.obj (op U)) (a : R₂.obj.obj (op U)),
        (Φ F).hom
          (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₂.obj U x hx a
          ⊗ₜ[TopCat.Presheaf.stalk (C := CommRingCat.{u}) (X := X) R₁.obj x,
            ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat x).map α.hom).hom]
            TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) F.val.presheaf U x hx s) =
          TopCat.Presheaf.germ (C := Ab.{u}) (X := X) (changeOfRingsPresheaf α F).presheaf U x hx
            (a ⊗ₜ[R₁.obj.obj (op U), (α.hom.app (op U)).hom] s))
